page: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon Platinum 8272CL processor operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. It provides 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores using symmetric multithreading (2 threads per core). Cache allocation includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and bit manipulation primitives (BMI2, ADX, FMA).

Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio (4.0 GB per vCPU). In benchmark testing, the memory subsystem achieved 82.97 GB/sec in uncached 256 MB sequential read throughput and 45.16 GB/sec in sequential write throughput. The instance includes no local ephemeral storage, requiring attached network volumes for persistent and temporary data storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with 0 GPUs assigned to the configuration.

Benchmark metrics reflect consistent mid-tier compute and memory throughput typical of Cascade Lake server architectures. The processor achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 7,938.0 and a single-core score of 1,269.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 15,671.52. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reached 39.96 GB/sec, while static web serving throughput reached 12.04 GB/sec. Redis SET throughput attained 13.89 million operations per second. CPU-bound machine learning tasks demonstrate performance limits, such as a weak prompt processing rate of 22.86 tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

The D16_v4 offers balanced cost efficiency for standard multi-threaded cloud deployments that do not require high-speed scratch disks or specialized matrix accelerators. The absence of bundled local storage lowers base infrastructure overhead while leaving persistent disk management to remote services. Workload fits include enterprise application servers, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, continuous integration build nodes, web serving fleets, and general data processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure D16_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 64.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Built on an x86_64 architecture with 8 physical cores and 2 threads per core, the processor supports AVX-512 VNNI instructions and features a 35 MB L3 cache. The instance contains no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying entirely on network-attached storage for disk operations. Standardized benchmarks place its multi-core compute and memory bandwidth in the middle performance tier, highlighted by 13.89 million Redis SET operations per second and 12.04 GB/sec static web throughput. With a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio, the D16_v4 is suited for enterprise web serving, relational databases, continuous integration workers, and containerized business services.
